tagline: Up the Pacolet beside the steepest main-line grade the country had.
intro: US 176 starts at the South Carolina line in Tryon, in the thermal belt that is generally free of dew and frost, and climbs to Saluda along the Pacolet River, crossing it again and again.

The railroad came up the same valley. The best route Charles Pearson could find for the Asheville and Spartanburg line up the Blue Ridge front followed the Pacolet, and it made the Saluda Grade, the steepest standard-gauge main line in the country, about 600 feet of climb in under three miles. The grade was infamous for runaway trains, and trains going up were allowed to run faster than trains coming down. The line has been out of service since 2001.

moments.title: Tryon
moments.text: Tryon was the birthplace of Eunice Waymon, known to the world as Nina Simone, and a bronze of her by Zenos Frudakis stands in the downtown plaza named for her.

moments.title: Pearson's Falls
moments.text: A glen off the highway named for Charles Pearson, the engineer who found the railroad its route, where a short trail climbs to a 90-foot waterfall.

moments.title: Saluda
moments.text: The town sits at the top of the grade, its Main Street at 2,097 feet, and had only two houses until the railroad arrived in 1878.
